title: Generalized hidden shift

problem.name: Generalized hidden shift
problem.statement_latex: Given injective functions $f_b:\mathbb Z_N\to S$ for $b\in\{0,\ldots,M-1\}$ satisfying $f_b(x)=f_0(x+bs)$, recover $s\in\mathbb Z_N$. Access to $(b,x)\mapsto f_b(x)$ is coherent.
problem.statement_text: Given injective functions $f_b:\mathbb Z_N\to S$ for $b\in\{0,\ldots,M-1\}$ satisfying $f_b(x)=f_0(x+bs)$, recover $s\in\mathbb Z_N$. Access to $(b,x)\mapsto f_b(x)$ is coherent.

strength.description_latex: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(\log N)$ time by Childs--van Dam when $M>N^\varepsilon$ for a fixed $\varepsilon>0$, using a pretty-good measurement and a lattice-point subroutine.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(\log N)$ time by Childs–van Dam when $M>N^\varepsilon$ for a fixed $\varepsilon>0$, using a pretty-good measurement and a lattice-point subroutine.

classical.headline_latex: Collision-based classical hidden-shift recovery uses $\widetilde O(\sqrt N)$ oracle calls; distinct oracle labels hide the shift until cross-function collisions occur.
